about: PROPOSED, UNSIGNED. One Proofline task, XC-110: external modes for R16a and R24, so the tier-1 run queue (XC-98) exercises them against a project's public testnet endpoint with unpaid requests only: five GETs with a malformed PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (R24) and one HEAD (R16a) that is sent off loopback only with the operator's permission (--operator-permission, the devnet runner's convention; on the form, the optional consent.unpaid_head box). Tier 1 grows from 9 to 11 checks within eight requests a run, at least 5 s apart. Owner's go 2026-10-25T21:22Z; sys confirmed no overlap at 21:27Z. Nothing here is binding until the owner key signs it into proofline.json.

tasks.title: External modes for R16a and R24 in the tier-1 queue: one unpaid HEAD with the operator's permission and five malformed-header GETs against the public testnet endpoint

tasks.description: Tier 1 (XC-98) grows from 9 to 11 checks. src/x402conf/external.py ports ts/src/head-unpaid.ts and ts/src/header.ts to Python, graded the same way, and `x402conf resource` gains --malformed-header (R24: one unpaid GET per malformed PAYMENT-SIGNATURE value, the same five values as MALFORMED_HEADERS in ts/src/header.ts, in the same order) and --unpaid-head (R16a: one unpaid HEAD; it passes on 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED offer or on 405 without PAYMENT-RESPONSE). Both reuse the GET that P1-P7 already sent and go through the run's pacer: at least 5 s apart off loopback, and a request over --max-requests is not sent and the check is reported skipped. A HEAD is not a GET, so off loopback it is sent only with --operator-permission <ref>, the devnet runner's convention for the operator's written permission, which the results record; without it R16a is skipped and the rest still runs. `x402conf-svm live` follows the same rule (on loopback it still grades P1-P7, R16a and R24 in 7 requests, XC-88). The 'Add or update my row' form gains an optional box, 'also allow one unpaid HEAD request per tier-1 run', stored as consent.unpaid_head; that box is the operator's permission, and the queue's `run` job passes the row's consent issue as --operator-permission only when it is ticked. The run job sends at most eight requests (P1-P7 and P9 on one GET, P10 on one GET of /.well-known/x402, R24 on five GETs, R16a on one HEAD), all unpaid, no facilitator call, no mainnet, zero spend, and never checks out the project's code. An external check the run did not reach (R16a without permission) counts as needing the self-hosted run. The example row becomes 8/9, '9 exercised / 2 NA / 68 needs self-hosted'. XC-90's extra R24 values, once signed, land in both lists together; criterion AC03 keeps them equal.

stop_rules: If a criterion cannot pass, STOP and report what blocks it, what was tried and what is needed. Never weaken a criterion, skip a test or raise a timeout to make it pass.

Testnet only: never use a mainnet CAIP-2 id as a payment target, never fund a key with anything but testnet faucet tokens, never call a hosted facilitator; every facilitator under test is the loopback double or my own instance on 127.0.0.1.

Zero spend and unpaid only: if a check would need a payment, a signature, a facilitator call or a request other than GET or the one permitted HEAD off loopback, STOP and report. Never send the HEAD off loopback without --operator-permission, and never more than eight requests a run.

Opt-in only: nothing about a project is committed (no row, no name in a table, no evidence, no badge) until it accepts through the 'Add or update my row' form or a pull request, with the consent recorded there. The outreach list is private and never committed. If a criterion seems to need a row for a project that has not accepted, STOP and report.
